messages.subject: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
messages.subject_clean: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
I have just downloaded and reordered the NCEP files as already suggested in this group.
There is an option for micro_ncep to read these local files. I am wondering if this is also possible with rhe runauto function?
How can I tell the runauto function to use the locally stored NCEP files?
Any help is greatly appreciated.
Best regards
Felix

messages.subject: Re: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
messages.subject_clean: Runauto function with locally downloaded NCEP files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Felix,

If you make your own version of runauto and change the line:

    micronmr <- micro_ncep(dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
        dem = r, dem2 = dem, LAI = 0, loc = loc, Usrhyt = hgt2,
        Refhyt = 2, coastal = coastal, reanalysis = reanalysis2,
        DEP = dep, save = save, hourlydata = hourlydata, dailyprecip = dailyprecip,
        weather.elev = weather.elev, cad.effects = cad.effects)

to

    micronmr <- micro_ncep(dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
        dem = r, dem2 = dem, LAI = 0, loc = loc, Usrhyt = hgt2,
        Refhyt = 2, coastal = coastal, reanalysis = reanalysis2,
        DEP = dep, save = save, hourlydata = hourlydata, dailyprecip = dailyprecip,
        weather.elev = weather.elev, cad.effects = cad.effects, spatial = 'your ncep data location')

I think it will work.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: micro_era5 and micro_ncep change
messages.body_plain:
Also when I made this change initially, I forgot about some subsequent code that caused a rather big problem (hourly rain vector became one value, zero!). I fixed that problem this morning so I think it's all working properly now.

On Monday, July 25, 2022 at 5:24:04 PM UTC+10 NicheMapR wrote:
> Hi everyone,
> I wanted to alert you to a change I've made to micro_era5 and micro_ncep to prevent them from getting stuck in endless loops in some circumstances. The short story is it won't make any difference to your calculations other than preventing the endless loops.
>
> The longer story is that I found that in some places the integrator was having difficulty finding a solution on days with a relatively large daily precipitation. In the microclimate model, the precipitation meant to fall daily at midnight. However, because the input data for micro_ncep and micro_era5 can start at times other than midnight, depending on the timezone (because it is based on UTC), there were situations where the precipitation was falling when there was high solar radiation. I've fixed it by putting the daily rainfall into the hourly rainfall input vector, on the hours that are local solar midnight.
>
> Hope that makes sense. The change is presently only on the github version.
>
> All the best,
> Mike

Hi Mike,
thanks a lot for your fast answer. I added the  "spatial = 'my ncep data location'" line in the
micronmr <- micro_ncep part within the runauto function, but it does not work for me.
Here is the place where the micro_ncep function is used within the runauto function.

...
 } else hgt2 <- hgt
  dep <- c(0, dep)
  loc <- c(long, lat)
  dem[dem == zmin] <- NA
  r[r == zmin] <- NA

  micronmr <- micro_ncep(dstart = dstart, dfinish = dfinish,
                         dem = r, dem2 = dem, LAI = 0, loc = loc, Usrhyt = hgt2,
                         Refhyt = 2, coastal = coastal, reanalysis = reanalysis2,
                         DEP = dep, save = save, hourlydata = hourlydata, dailyprecip = dailyprecip,

                         weather.elev = weather.elev, cad.effects = cad.effects, spatial = "D:/global_climate/ncep/")
  ma <- micronmr$microclima.out
  hourlydata <- ma$hourlydata
  tme <- as.POSIXlt(tme + 0, tz = "UTC")
  nmrout <- as.data.frame(micronmr$metout)
  rwind <- ma$hourlyradwind
  netrad = (1 - 0.15) * rwind$swrad - 0.98 * hourlydata$netlong *
    rwind$skyviewfact * (1 - rwind$canopyfact)
  cat("Paramaterising model using NicheMapR \n")
...

Is it possible to keep the runauto function or was your suggestion to use the micro_ncep function instead and transform it?
Best regards
Felix

thanks a lot, it works now.
I am using a for-loop to run the simulation for my study area for several months. Until now, I had the runauto function in another R script and was accessing it using the source command.
As I put everything in one script it worked.

But now I am facing a new problem. It runs the simulation for the first 6 months of every year (2010-2019), but then it stops abprutly.
I get this error for July:
Calculating summary data
Error in if (P>0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
I have no idea why this error occurs, as there seems to be no problem for the other months.

Best regards
Felix

Hi Felix and Mike,

>From some of my troubleshooting with these functions, perhaps this may provide a lead of where the issue/bug is in the code: that error suggests that at some point a vector was made completely NA, before being handed to a logical statement-- the error itself is thrown by the logical statement, and in my experience from troubleshooting microclima, the vector was made NA when the mean() is taken of an upstream vector that has at least one NA. As an example, see this line 1087 on the micro_ncep() function <https://streaklinks.com/BJqs5Qo6-qsRIOlPqQGbTGj_/https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fmrke%2FNicheMapR%2Fblob%2F7a66f23cf2662674c8c573813df9fd480e75b3d1%2FR%2Fmicro_ncep.R%23L1087>: in this line, if there are any NAs in the vector `VPD_diff`, then mean(VPD_diff) will just return NA, which will make VPDhr also NA, and so on.

So Felix, you might want to check if there are any NA values in any of your data inputs. Mike, in some of Ilya's functions I've added an argument `na.rm = TRUE` to any uses of mean(), min(), max(), and sometimes an informative error of "found NAs in vector X", as ways to prevent or trap this error. But I haven't had the chance to pull request any such changes to NicheMapR functions.

Best,
Dave

messages.subject: How to simulate drought for a given location
messages.subject_clean: How to simulate drought for a given location
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,
Is there a way to simulate drought with the micro_global function for a given location?

There are many definitions of drought in the literature. For example, when there is a prolonged time with less than average precipitation, or an increase in vapor pressure deficit (VPD). I was thinking of changing the VPD given the non-standard lack of rainfall for a long period is a bit subjective. Some use time and others use below-average rainfall.

I had a look at the micro_global function on GitHub (https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/blob/master/R/micro_global.R) but there was no option for VPD. Any advice or recommendations that could help simulate drought?

Much appreciated,
Nicholas

--

Nicholas C. Wu | PhD

Postdoctoral Research Fellow

Animal Ecology Lab | Hawkesbury Institute for the Environment

Western Sydney University, NSW 2753 | Australia

E: nichola...@gmail.com | M: +61 409 456 802 | W: http://wunicholas.wix.com/home

messages.subject_clean: How to simulate drought for a given location
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nicholas,

Reducing the rainfall would seem to be the most obvious way to impose a drought though. It really depends on what process you're trying to modify for what species.

Is it altering the water intake? That would then require a prediction of food water content and the possibility of drinking from rain. You could use the plantgro function to simulate plant water content as a function of soil water potential.

Is it altering water loss? That would be driven by atmospheric water content, i.e. vapour pressure/humidity.

To alter the vapour pressure, you'd need to modify the relative humidity coming from the global_climate.nc <http://global_climate.nc> file that is used as input. You'd have to convert it first to vapour pressure with the WETAIR function, drop it by the factor you're after, and then convert it back to relative humidity to then be passed to the microclimate model. That would require modifying the micro_global function.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: functional response
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am working with my internship tutor on an R-Shiny application, based on the DEB_euler and DEB fonctions, whose goal is to simulate aquaculture waste (food, faeces...).

As we are dealing with farmed fishes, we were wondering how we could model the different practices of fish farmers regarding the management of fish diets. Indeed, farmers can overfeed or underfeed animals according to their development stage in order to improve growth performances.

Our question is the following:  as it refers to the equation f(X)=X/(K+X) can the functional response f in the DEB_euler fonction be larger than 1 ? Or should we model an overfed individual with f=1 ?

For now, we only found about f < 1  in the scientific literature and implemented it into our farm model with no difficulty. However, we can't find any results based on f > 1.

Thank you for your time.

Kind regards,

Léanne

messages.subject: Re: functional response
messages.body_plain:
Hi Léanne,

Good question. You can make f > 1, and I've seen this done in some parameter estimation routines,  but that is the same as increasing the maximum specific assimilation rate parameter {p_Am}. So it will mean your fish will grow bigger. It won't become fatter for the same size (i.e., storing an excess of e.g. fat).

All the best,
Mike
